name: Iris Mauve
lede: Iris Mauve is a pale, yellowish pink named for the iris flower, common in Indian paintings in our archive.

sections.title: A flower word, not the dye
sections.body: The library records Iris Mauve from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 3 B 7, first recorded 1926 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[shell-pink]], [[shell-pink]], [[tussore]] and [[almond]], at 2.6, 2.6, 3.3 and 3.7 ΔE [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 84, chroma 11, hue 66 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "pale yellowish pink" block, Munsell 5.6YR 8.3/2.0, [1]. 6, 2.6, 3.3 and 3.7 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 771 of 23,781 paintings, 3.24 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 537 [2]. That makes it more common than 83 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 81 of 1,674 paintings, at 4.8 percent of that century's paintings, 2.0 times the expected rate, and it is over-represented in Indian paintings, 2.1 times expected, 91 of 721 [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light, in 55 percent of its appearances [2].

Xugu is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 16 works here, 7.4 times the baseline [2]. The earliest match is dated 1000; that is 930 years before the name's own first record, in 1930, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: pairs the iris flower with the word mauve, though the color itself is a pale neutral, not purplish
origin.source: Maerz & Paul, A Dictionary of Color (1930)
